title: Germany declares war on Portugal
summary: Portugal requisitioned the German and Austrian merchant ships interned in the Tagus and other ports on 23 February 1916, at Britain's request and under the terms of the alliance; Germany declared war on 9 March. Portugal was already fighting German colonial forces in Angola and Mozambique, but the declaration brought it formally into the European war and made possible the expeditionary corps sent to Flanders the following year. The Democrats around Afonso Costa had pressed for belligerence, partly to secure the colonies and the country's standing at the peace, and the war they obtained divided the republic more deeply than anything else it did. It is in the atlas as the decision from which the Lys, the Sidónio Pais coup and much of the army's later politics follow.
